close_reason: Deferred: optimization benefits hypothetical SQL backend; reference MemoryBackend doesn't see the difference. Re-open when a SQL consumer reports the latency.
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/emoji.rs:481-498 (update pre-fetch) and 595-612 (destroy pre-fetch).

Each update or destroy entry triggers a separate get_objects::<CustomEmoji>(caller, account_id, Some(&[id]), None) to learn the spaceId for the authorization gate. For a batch of N updates, that's N round-trips.

Cleanly batchable:
1. Collect all distinct ids in the update + destroy lists at the top of the function.
2. Single get_objects::<CustomEmoji>(caller, account_id, Some(&all_ids), None) — backends MAY push this down to a single SQL IN clause.
3. Build HashMap<Id, Option<Id>> of id -> space_id, then look up in O(1) per gate.

The MemoryBackend doesn't notice (HashMap reads are cheap), but a production SQL-backed implementation processing a 100-emoji destroy batch issues 100 round-trips today vs 1 batched.

Not P0/P1 because: typical batches are small, and CustomEmoji/set is rarely on the hot path. Filing for future tuning.
title: CustomEmoji/set update + destroy do an extra get_objects per entry; could batch the pre-fetch
